title: AQUAH: Automatic Quantification and Unified Agent in Hydrology
authors: Songkun Yan; Zhi Li; Siyu Zhu; Yixin Wen; Mofan Zhang; Mengye Chen; Jie Cao; Yang Hong
agentic_techniques: tool use; planning and decomposition; multi-agent orchestration (8 specialized agents: Context Parser, Dataset Retriever, Perceptor, OutletSelector, ParamInitializer, Operator, Report Writer, Feedback Reflector); retrieval of external geospatial/Earth-observation data; code execution (Python geospatial libraries)
architecture: pipeline-with-agent: LLM interface converts natural-language input into structured simulation instructions; tool-executor layer runs Python geospatial libraries and a hydrologic model (CREST); sequential specialized agents handle retrieval, parameterization, execution and reporting
evaluation_method: two-tier evaluation combining automated GPT-o3 grading and domain-expert hydrologist scoring (10-point scale, four dimensions: Model Completeness, Simulation Results, Reasonableness, Clarity), across ten independent initialisations per model, comparing three LLM backbones (claude-4-opus, Claude-Sonnet-4, and at least one other)
baseline: comparison across LLM backbones (claude-4-opus vs Claude-Sonnet-4 vs others), not against a non-agentic hydrologic-modeling baseline
reported_result: claude-4-opus achieves the highest average score (7.01) across four criteria; Claude-Sonnet-4 shows the most consistent (narrow, uniformly positive) score distribution across ten runs; authors report AQUAH completes cold-start simulations and produces analyst-ready documentation without manual intervention
maturity_claimed: AQUAH autonomously retrieves required terrain, forcing and gauge data, configures a hydrologic model, runs the simulation, and generates a self-contained PDF report from a natural-language prompt, with results judged by hydrologists as clear, transparent and physically plausible (abstract)
maturity_demonstrated: M3 prototype on real data: evaluated on named U.S. basins using real Earth-observation/gauge data (MRMS precipitation, USGS discharge, HydroSHEDS terrain) retrospectively; not used operationally
author_stated_limitations: authors state further calibration and validation are still needed for operational deployment; the prototype depends on publicly hosted data and inference services (USGS, MRMS, a cloud LLM), so regional access limits or outages could reduce functionality; discerning human water regulation from natural flow remains challenging for current mainstream LLMs

title: GeoMind: An Agentic Workflow for Lithology Classification with Reasoned Tool Invocation
authors: Mingyue Cheng; Yitong Zhou; Jiahao Wang; Qingyang Mao; Qi Liu
agentic_techniques: tool use with reasoned/justified invocation; planning (Planner-Executor-Reflector loop); domain-adaptive supervised fine-tuning of the backbone LLM; process-level reward shaping for intermediate reasoning steps
architecture: single-agent pipeline with internal modularity: perception module (raw well logs to semantic trends), reasoning module (lithology hypotheses from multi-source evidence), analysis module (verification against stratigraphic constraints), coordinated by a Planner-Executor-Reflector control loop
evaluation_method: benchmarked on four public well-log datasets (SEAM, Facies, FORCE, GeoLink) against classical ML (XGBoost), deep time-series classifiers (InceptionTime, MOMENT), and LLM-based baselines (GPT4TS) using weighted precision/recall/F1; held-out test sets defined by well identity
baseline: XGBoost; InceptionTime; MOMENT; GPT4TS; other domain-specific methods
reported_result: GeoMind achieves the strongest or near-strongest weighted F1 across all four datasets, with roughly +5.7 F1 points over the next-best on FORCE and +3.4 on Facies; produces fewer anomalously short lithology-interval runs than XGBoost and GPT4TS, reducing fragmentation by up to 27.9%
maturity_claimed: experiments on four benchmark well-log datasets demonstrate that GeoMind consistently outperforms strong baselines in classification performance while providing transparent and traceable decision-making processes (abstract)
maturity_demonstrated: M2 benchmark prototype: evaluated on four reusable, community well-log benchmark datasets (SEAM, Facies, FORCE, GeoLink) containing real logged data but site-agnostic; benchmark_also not applicable (already the benchmark tier)
author_stated_limitations: authors state the system was trained and evaluated on a machine with 4x NVIDIA A800 GPUs 'due to the additional memory and compute overhead,' implying non-trivial compute cost; no explicit discussion of failure modes or untested settings found in the extracted text
